Triage: lands in `packages/cli` (the `-t app` init template + the init-time scaffold validation) → `domain:cli`, type Bug, promoted to `pm:queue`. Dedup: searched `security-owd-unset` / scaffold-compile family — no open duplicate (#9698 is a different lint gap; #7503 closed, different rule).

Added `target:v17`: this is a tier-① release blocker by the board's binary test — the published `17.0.0` quickstart path (`init` → `dev`) is dead on first run for every new user today, measured on the npm `latest` tag.

Both suggested fixes belong to one card: (1) template declares `sharingModel: 'private'` (one line, the rule's own recommended default — restores the declared on-ramp, no contract change); (2) init's scaffold validation runs the author-time rule set so template regressions fail at generation. Fix (2) is validation-strengthening, not an accept-set expansion.

Size/model suggestion: S–M, `mode:subagent`.

## Premise re-verified on `origin/main` — the defect is live here, not only on published 17.0.0

The card measured npm `latest` = `17.0.0`. That is a different tree from `main`, so I re-derived rather than assuming the report transfers:

| control: `create-objectstack`'s `blank` template `note.object.ts` | **1** — so the property exists and is used elsewhere; the zero above is a real absence, not a broken query |
| where the `app` template actually lives | **inline in `init.ts`** (`srcFiles` at `:154`, `:228`, `:283`) — ⚠️ **not** in `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/`, where a directory scan looks first and finds nothing |
| the init-time validator | `init.ts:541` `printStep('Validating scaffold...')` → `:552` `printSuccess('Scaffold validated…')` |

⚠️ That third row is the trap worth naming: searching `templates/` for the `app` template returns **nothing**, and a dev who stops there could conclude the card is stale. It is not — the template is emitted from a `srcFiles` map inside `init.ts`.

Where the template and validator actually live, re-derived on `origin/main` (line numbers as found, before my edits): `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` — `TEMPLATES` map opens at `:94`; the three `srcFiles` maps at `:154` (`app`), `:228` (`plugin`), `:283` (`empty`, which is `{}`); the src-file write loop at `:495`; the init-time validator at `:541` `printStep('Validating scaffold...')` through `:552` `printSuccess('Scaffold validated…')`. The PM's indicative line numbers were accurate. `git grep -c sharingModel` in that file was indeed 0, against 1 in `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/src/objects/note.object.ts:26` — that control was verified rather than trusted, and the `blank` template does conform.

The rule set `dev` runs, traced rather than assumed: `dev.ts:192` spawns `os compile`; `compile.ts:177` calls `authoringRulesFor('build')`. That is why the scaffold self-test is pinned to `'build'` and why the pin test asserts the coupling (`SCAFFOLD_RULE_COMMAND === 'build'`) instead of restating the string.

## 1. `content/docs/` — no edit belongs in this PR, and it is not a deferral

I did not skip it and I am not calling it out-of-scope: I checked, and **the premise does not hold**. `examples.mdx` does not reproduce the object I am fixing.

The single `my_app_item` hit is `content/docs/getting-started/examples.mdx:365`, and it is inside a `Callout` describing the scaffold's **file layout**, in prose:

> `os init` scaffolds a minimal starter, not this full tree. It emits `objectstack.config.ts` plus a single object under `src/objects/{namespace}_item.ts` (e.g. `my_app_item.ts`) with a matching barrel `src/objects/index.ts`.

There is no object literal on that page — nothing a reader could copy, and therefore nothing that would fail the author-time rules. My change adds one property *inside* the object literal and alters no file name, path or barrel, so every claim in that Callout is still exactly true after the fix. Editing it would mean adding a `sharingModel` mention to a passage that is about directory structure.

**My own enumeration for the same shape under a different name** (your query was `my_app_item`; these are mine):

| query | result |
| --- | --- |
| `_item` across `content/docs/**` excluding `releases/` | 20 hits, **all unrelated** — `list_item` action locations, `min_items`/`max_items` error keys, `order_line_item` |
| `'archived'` (the scaffold's distinctive status triple `draft`/`active`/`archived`) | 10 hits, all enum/reference tables for unrelated objects |
| pages documenting `os init` | 4: `releases/v17.mdx` (read-only), `your-first-project.mdx`, `examples.mdx`, `deployment/cli.mdx` |
| object literal in `your-first-project.mdx` | **already correct** — `:153` `sharingModel: 'private',  // org-wide default — an explicit, authored decision` |
| `os init` section of `deployment/cli.mdx` | a template table, no object literal |
| `Scaffold validated` / `Validating scaffold` anywhere in `content/docs/` | **0 hits** — the behaviour and message I changed are documented nowhere, so nothing went stale. Control: `author-time rule` returns 5 pages, so the grep works |

I also considered `deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`, whose "The one gate, four doors" section enumerates `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` / runtime-publish. I deliberately did **not** add a fifth door. `init` does not open a new gate over authored metadata — it self-tests the CLI's own generated output using the `build` door's existing rule set, and the user hits that same door moments later on `dev`. Listing it beside the four would misdescribe it as a surface authors need to reason about.

⛔ `content/docs/releases/` untouched, as instructed. For the record, the drift check names 23 pages for this diff (`node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json origin/main`), 4 of them release pages — advisory "these docs name something you touched", not a mandate, and none of the 23 is made stale by this change.

**Nothing to file as a follow-up from this item** — there is no drift here to preserve.

## 2. Declared-surface addition — naming it, per your note

This PR adds one file beyond the declared surface (`init.ts`'s two regions + its test + `.changeset/**`):

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/scaffold-validate.ts`** (new, 130 lines)

Reason: `init`'s self-test now needs the normalize → lower-callables → Zod-parse → registry pipeline that `compile.ts` runs. Leaving it inline in `init.ts` would have put a fourth copy of that pipeline in the tree and, more importantly, left the pin test with no way to exercise the *real* self-test — it would have had to re-implement the checking, which is the drift the pin exists to catch. The module exports `validateScaffold` (loader + rules) and `SCAFFOLD_RULE_COMMAND` (pinned to `'build'`, asserted by the test rather than restated).

Agreed on the risk analysis: a new file in the same package collides with nobody, so this is a record-honesty matter, not a code one. Two smaller surface notes in the same spirit:

- `init.ts` gained an exported `writeTemplateSrcFiles` (the step-4 loop, extracted unchanged) so the pin test generates through the real emitter. Same region as the declared template surface.
- `init.ts` line count grew by ~90; the two edited regions are the ones you named.

## 3. Zone 2 per-template result — unchanged, restated because you asked for it explicitly

Measured through the real rule runner (41 `build` rules), before any fix:

| template | pre-fix | post-fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app` | 1 error — `security-owd-unset` at `objects[0].sharingModel` | 0 |
| `plugin` | 1 error — same rule, same path | 0 |
| `empty` | 0 (emits no objects) | 0 |

**Your Zone 2 assumption #1 is falsified**: `app` was not the only template that trips the set. `plugin` was in the identical state and is fixed here — same defect class, same mechanical fix, pinned by the same authored baseline.

Filed unassigned, no labels, with the two repair directions and a note that it needs a product call rather than a mechanical fix.
